entities.name: CVE-2023-3519
entities.evidence: CVE-2023-3519 is an unauthenticated RCE vulnerability affecting the following versions of NetScaler

entities.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
entities.evidence: In July 2023, a critical infrastructure organization reported to CISA that threat actors may have exploited a zero-day vulnerability in NetScaler ADC to implant a webshell on their non-production NetScaler ADC appliance

entities.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
entities.evidence: In August 2023, CISA received TTPs and IOCs from an additional victim and third parties. The actors implanted a webshell, gained root level access to the compromised system, and performed discovery against the Active Directory (AD)

entities.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
entities.evidence: As part of their initial exploit chain [T1190], the threat actors uploaded a TGZ file [T1105] containing a generic webshell [T1505.003], discovery script [TA0007], and setuid binary [T1548.001] on the ADC appliance and conducted SMB scanning on the subnet [T1046].

entities.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
entities.evidence: The actors used the webshell for AD enumeration [T1016] and to exfiltrate AD data [TA0010].

entities.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
entities.evidence: The actors used the following command to encrypt discovery data collected via openssl in “tar ball” [T1560.001]: tar -czvf - /var/tmp/all.txt | openssl des3 -salt -k <> -out /var/tmp/test.tar.gz. (A “tar ball” is a compressed and zipped file used by threat actors for collection and exfiltration.)

entities.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
entities.evidence: Exfiltrated collected data by uploading as an image file [T1036.008] to a web-accessible path [T1074]: cp /var/tmp/test.tar.gz /netscaler/ns_gui/vpn/medialogininit.png.

entities.name: Network Service Discovery
entities.evidence: The actors attempted to: • Execute a subnet-wide curl command to identify what was accessible from within the network as well as potential lateral movement targets.

entities.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
entities.evidence: Verified outbound network connectivity with a ping command (ping -c 1 google.com) [T1016.001].

entities.name: CVE-2023-3519
entities.evidence: The actors’ other discovery activities were unsuccessful due to the critical infrastructure organization’s deployment of their NetScaler ADC appliance in a segmented environment.

entities.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
entities.evidence: The threat actors exploited CVE-2023-3519 to implant a webshell on the organization’s NetScaler ADC appliance.

entities.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
entities.evidence: The threat actors executed /bin/sh as root.

entities.name: Native API
entities.evidence: The threat actors executed /bin/sh via syscall.

entities.name: Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
entities.evidence: the victim observed communications with two pfSense IP addresses indicating the actor was using them for multi-hop proxying C2 traffic

entities.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification
entities.evidence: The webshell path was in a web accessible folder, and the actors’ modifications enabled them to run /bin/sh commands as root and enabled persistence because the webshell was run on every reboot [T1547].

entities.name: Indicator Removal
entities.evidence: After exfiltrating the files, the actors deleted them from the system [T1070.004] as well as some access logs, error logs, and authentication logs [T1070.002].

entities.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs

entities.evidence: After exfiltrating the files, the actors deleted them from the system [T1070.004] as well as some access logs, error logs, and authentication logs [T1070.002].

entities.name: Data Staged: Local Data Staging
entities.evidence: The actors also attempted to delete their artifacts [TA0005]. The actors deleted the authorization configuration file (/etc/auth.conf)—likely to prevent configured users (e.g., admin) from logging in remotely (e.g., CLI) [T1531].

entities.name: Protocol Tunneling
entities.evidence: Deployed LIGOLO-NG [5] tunneller with the filename the in the /tmp directory. LIGOLO-NG is a tunneller [T1572] written in Go that provides encrypted reverse TCP/TLS connections [T1573.002] to a remote host.

entities.name: Command and Control
entities.evidence: The threat actors appear to have used compromised pfSense devices to proxy C2 traffic to Victim 2.

entities.name: Obtain Capabilities: Tool
entities.evidence: The threat actors leveraged open source webshells [2] [4] and other publicly available tools, including a modified version of open-source SSH inject tool [3], LIGOLO-NG [5] tunneller, and NPS tunneller [6].
